node.label: Mary Douglas
node.date_label: Purity and Danger (1966) · The World of Goods, with Baron Isherwood (1979) · How Institutions Think (1986) · Lancaster interview on classification and the body (1987)
node.description: Studies classification, bodily symbolism and the social work of goods. In the selected 1987 interview, she places her account of the body within a Durkheimian classificatory conversation while resisting the interviewer’s imposed theoretical alternatives. The interviewer’s summaries and her responses remain distinct. Featherstone and Turner’s later introduction reads her collaboration with Baron Isherwood as locating consumption within systems of meaning rather than merely a division between necessities and luxuries. That particular named reading supplies the consumption claim; it does not become a new claim to have read the whole World of Goods.

proposed_edges.relationship: Examines the body as a resource for social classification, while distinguishing that project from the interviewer’s phenomenological framing.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own answers printed pp. 138–140, with pp. 133–134 editorial context and selected earlier biographical answers read. Does not attribute every interviewer formulation to Douglas or certify her broad dismissal of chronological approaches as correct.

proposed_edges.relationship: With Baron Isherwood, treats goods within social systems of meaning rather than reducing consumption to necessities versus luxuries.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Explicitly mediated through Mike Featherstone and Bryan S. Turner’s substantive introduction, printed p. 134; original World of Goods unread. Coauthorship retained; their 1978 bibliographic date is not substituted for separately checked original 1979.
